Question B-007-004-009.

Why the correct answer is right: A wide signal occupies more spectrum, so multipath can affect one portion differently from another. That makes selective fading more noticeable as transmitted bandwidth increases.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "It is the same for both wide and narrow bandwidths": Equal effect ignores that a wide signal gives the fading more frequency range to act on unevenly.
- sourceIndex 2: "Only the receiver bandwidth determines the selective fading effect": Receiver filtering matters to what you hear, but the transmitted bandwidth and propagation path also determine how much of the signal can fade selectively.
- sourceIndex 3: "It is more pronounced at narrow bandwidths": Narrow signals are less likely to show different fading across their occupied spectrum, so this reverses the usual effect.
